Formulation  
Middle-aged man with chronic medical comorbidities including type 2 diabetes and hypertension presents with mild low mood and physical symptoms consistent with an acute viral illness. Predisposing factors include chronic health conditions and being overweight. Precipitating factors include recent onset of respiratory symptoms and feeling run-down. Perpetuating factors are low energy and poor sleep. Protective factors include stable social support and employment. No significant mental health history or risks identified.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Low mood and malaise secondary to acute viral illness  
- Patient Goal(s): Feel physically better and regain usual energy and motivation  
- Clinical Goal(s): Resolution of viral symptoms and improvement in mood and functioning  
- Actions (Patient): Rest, maintain hydration, monitor symptoms, use Paracetamol for fever/sweats, reduce alcohol intake, continue efforts to cut down smoking  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide advice on symptomatic management, supply delayed antibiotic prescription (Amoxicillin 1 tablet TID) if symptoms worsen or no improvement in 24-48 hours, review in one week if no improvement  

Secondary Problem: Type 2 diabetes mellitus  
- Patient Goal(s): Maintain adequate glycemic control  
- Clinical Goal(s): Continue Metformin and monitor blood glucose as per standard management  
- Actions (Patient): Continue current diabetes medication and monitoring  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Regular review and management of diabetes as part of chronic care (not addressed in this consultation)  

Tertiary Problem: Hypertension  
- Patient Goal(s): Achieve blood pressure control  
- Clinical Goal(s): Continue antihypertensive therapy, monitor blood pressure  
- Actions (Patient): Continue Lisinopril as prescribed  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Monitor blood pressure; adjust therapy as indicated (no change in current consultation)  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention  
- Education Given: Yes. Topics covered: Viral illness symptom management, importance of rest and hydration, when to commence antibiotics, smoking cessation support, limiting alcohol intake  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increasing shortness of breath, fever persisting or worsening beyond 48 hours, ongoing malaise  
- Coping Strategies: Rest, fluid intake, use of Paracetamol for fever, gradual return to normal activities  

Consent, Coordination & Review  
- Patient Consent to Plan: Implied consent given during consultation  
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded  
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: Not recorded  
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not recorded  
- Review Date: One week if no symptom improvement; sooner if deterioration

- Internal conflicts from the transcript: Minor conflict regarding diabetes type (patient initially hesitated but stated type 2)  
- Transcript quality notes: Audio quality clear; some sections conversational with anecdotal information but clinical details adequately documented
